nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Co(OH)₂ shows large nanosheets (~10 μm) with smooth surface densely aligned on NF; NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ shows smaller (~0.4 μm) 2D nanosheet array with rougher surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the SEM and TEM images of the NF/Co(OH)₂ Figures 1b-d, S1, and S2), the nanosheets with smooth surface are densely aligned on the NF substrate... Regarding the NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ from the SEM and TEM images in Figures 1e,f, and S5, it also presents similar 2D nanosheet array architecture, while the nanosheets (~0.4 μm) are much smaller in size relative to those of NF/Co(OH)₂ (~10 μm).

nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ nanosheet surface is rougher with multitude of amorphous regions; lattice fringe of 0.27 nm assigned to (100) plane of α-Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the zoom-in TEM image exhibits that the nanosheet surface is rougher (Figure 1g). In addition, the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Figure 1h, the lattice fringe with distance of 0.27 nm and the corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) pattern are assigned to (100) plane of α-Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Co(OH)₂ exhibits characteristic diffraction peaks of β-Co(OH)₂ (PDF 30-0443); NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ shows diffraction peaks of α-Co(OH)₂ (PDF 46-0605) with (003) peak at ~9.1° shifted to lower angle due to MoO₄²⁻ intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And its XRD pattern exhibits characteristic diffraction peaks of β-Co(OH)₂ PDF card no.30-0443) (Figure 2a)... the XRD pattern of NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ presents diffraction peaks of α-Co(OH)₂ PDF card no.46-0605... The peak at ~9.1° is attributed to the (003) plane of the α-Co(OH)₂, notably, due to intercalation of large-sized MoO₄²⁻ in the interlayer space, such (003) peak shifts to lower angle.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Co(OH)₂ confirms formation of β-Co(OH)₂; NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ shows α-Co(OH)₂ peaks plus characteristic MoO₄²⁻ peaks at 334, 811, 879, and 931 cm⁻¹; no Co-O-Mo bond peaks evidencing intercalation rather than doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the Raman spectrum further demonstrates the formation of β-Co(OH)₂ (Figure S4). Regarding the Raman spectrum of the NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ (Figure S4), apart from the peaks attributed to the α-Co(OH)₂, the peaks at 334, 811, 879, and 931 cm⁻¹ characteristic of MoO₄²⁻ can be observed, and no peaks assigned to Co-O-Mo bond emerges, evidencing MoO₄²⁻ intercalation rather than Mo species doping in the NF/MoCo(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Co(OH)₂ shows Co-O at 676 cm⁻¹, O-H stretching 3600-3200 cm⁻¹, bending 1634 cm⁻¹, CO₃²⁻ at 1379 cm⁻¹; NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ shows new Mo-O peak at 872 cm⁻¹ confirming MoO₄²⁻ incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectrum identifies the stretching vibration of CoO (676 cm⁻¹), and the peaks at 3600-3200 and 1634 cm⁻¹ are correlated with the O-H stretching and bending vibration, respectively... from the FTIR spectrum in Figure 2b, a new peak appears at 872 cm⁻¹ attributed to the stretching vibration of Mo-O bond appears, confirming MoO₄²⁻ incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ shows lattice fringe distance of 0.27 nm corresponding to (100) plane of α-Co(OH)₂ with multitude of amorphous regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: from the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Figure 1h, the lattice fringe with distance of 0.27 nm and the corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) pattern are assigned to (100) plane of α-Co(OH)₂. Of note, a multitude of amorphous regions are also observed in Mo-Co(OH)₂ nanosheet.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ shows uniform distribution of Co, Mo, and O elements in nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mappings display that Co, Mo, and O elements are uniformly distributed in the nanosheets (Figure 1i).

nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ has Co/Mo molar ratio of 1:0.523.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the molar ratio of Co/Mo is determined to be 1:0.523 through the inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ survey confirms Co, Mo, O presence; Mo 3d peaks at 234.7 eV and 231.8 eV indicate Mo⁶⁺; NF/Co(OH)₂ Co 2p shows Co³⁺ (780.3/796.2 eV) and Co²⁺ (782.4/797.8 eV); NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ Co 2p peaks positively shifted confirming MoO₄²⁻ intercalation modulates Co electronic structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The survey spectra of NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ demonstrate the existence of Co, Mo, and O elements (Figure S9). From the Mo 3d spectrum in Figure 2c, the peaks at 234.7 and 231.8 eV correspond to Mo⁶⁺ species... for the NF/Co(OH)₂, the peaks at 780.3 and 796.2 eV correspond to Co³⁺ species, and the peaks at 782.4 and 797.8 eV are assigned to Co²⁺ species. Of note, the peaks of Co species in NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ exhibit positive shift in binding energy compared to those of NF/Co(OH)₂, suggesting that MoO₄²⁻ intercalation can modulate surface electronic structure of Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows higher absorption edge for Mo-Co(OH)₂ vs Co(OH)₂ indicating Co electron depletion; FT-EXAFS shows Co-O (1.61 Å) and Co-O-Co (2.69 Å) bonds in both.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown the Co K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra in Figure 2e, relative to Co(OH)₂, the absorption edge of MoCo(OH)₂ is in higher energy, indicating the electron depletion of Co species after MoO₄²⁻ intercalation... Fourier-transformed k³χ(k) of Co K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FTEXAFS) presents that both Co(OH)₂ and Mo-Co(OH)₂ display Co-O (1.61 Å) and Co-O-Co (2.69 Å) bonds (Figure 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values are 36.0 mF cm⁻² for NF/Co(OH)₂ and 87.0 mF cm⁻² for NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ indicating MoO₄²⁻ intercalation exposes more active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Figures S19 and 5i, the Cdl values of NF/Co(OH)₂ and NF/Mo-Co(OH)₂ are calculated to be 36.0 and 87.0 mF cm⁻², respectively, proving that MoO₄²⁻ intercalation contributes to exposing more abundant catalytic sites.
